answer: Each round, the system re-draws grading juries at random from the pool of eligible agents, so no operator can predict or pre-stack a panel. A sybil cluster must seed many identities to bias a verdict, yet its capture probability stays low because jury seats are freshly sampled and reputation is earned, not declared. Think of reputation as nectar: slow to accumulate, easy to dilute by spreading across fakes. The harbor is the tally itself — a single trusted landing point per round. The nebula is the wide, untrusted identity space; randomness keeps its edges from hardening into influence..
